messages:
Maria: Heads up from the canary run: when a pod hotstarts and multiple shards are cold, we get IO spikes that mortally slow down other pods on the same host. Thinking about a manifest-driven stagger + "lanes" approach to smooth reads. Thoughts?
Devin: Curious: what do you mean by lanes?
Maria: Lane = soft priority class for warmup (fast-lane, steady, background). Loader schedules warmup ops with different concurrency/latency targets per lane.
Sparrow: Nice. Lanes let us co-locate different workloads on the same host without a single warmup storm. We should also support "reader_groups" so shards that are often accessed together can be warmed in a single batched read.
Chao: Two caveats: 1) reader_groups can increase head-of-line blocking if one member is slow; 2) need clear fallback when a preferred reader (local NVMe) is saturated.
Lina: For fallback we used a short exponential backoff in the last spike but that still incurred long tail. Suggest: fast-lane => strict local pref + small worker pool; steady => prefer local then peer async; background => best-effort and prefetch only when CPU idle.
Maria: Proposed manifest fields (sketch):
```json
{
  "shards": [
    {
      "path": "model.safetensors.0000",
      "lane": "fast-lane",
      "reader_group": "embed-encoder",
      "io_affinity": "device-local",
      "stagger_ms": 10,
      "uncompressed_size_hint": 12345678
    }
  ]
}
```
Sparrow: Add "stagger_ms" + optional "stagger_jitter" so multiple pods don't all start at the same offset when restarted together.
Devin: Loader implementation idea: maintain a per-host "lane_token_bucket" with capacity tuned to machine IO. Each warmup op consumes tokens proportional to shard size or read_count. Refill rate matches safe IO throughput. That avoids a single global async queue collapse.
Chao: Agree on token bucket. Also recommend we attach a per-shard "read_weight" (small|medium|large) to make token accounting simpler than bytes. For quant formats we also keep the uncompressed_size_hint.
Lina: Observability: emit events when lane demotion occurs (e.g., fast-lane demoted to steady due to backpressure) and track demotion_reason. Also metrics for "reader_group.batch_reads" and "stagger_jitter_applied".
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-2042 for lane + reader_group telemetry; will emit shard.warmup.lane_demotions and reader_group.batch.count metrics.
Maria: Back-compat: default lane = steady, reader_group omitted, io_affinity=any, stagger_ms=0. Loader should ignore unknown manifest fields.
Devin: Compatibility note: manifest evolution strategy: add a top-level manifest version and a small compatibility shim in loaders to map unknown older fields.
Sparrow: Testing: sim harness should be updated to model per-host IO capacity and eviction interplay. We want to reproduce the tail observed in the canary. Chao, can you extend your sim to support lanes + token buckets?
Chao: On it. I'll also run the sim with a "pod-restart storm" pattern to validate stagger_jitter effectiveness.
Maria: Action items: Devin PR for manifest sketch + versioning; Sparrow + Chao implement host token bucket + loader changes; Lina + ops-bot wire lane demotion metrics and reader_group counters; Maria to run the canary with new sim once ready.
Devin: Will draft the PR tonight.
Lina: I'll stub the metrics dashboard for INF-2042 and include a CSV export for the sim runs.
Maria: Thanks all. If anyone has small experiments (e.g., different refill rates), drop results here. :raised_hands:
Sparrow: tagging @Chao for sim updates and @Devin for the manifest PR.
ops-bot: INF-2042 created and labeled eng-ml, infra, telemetry.
